root.name: Queen's Indian Defense: Buerger Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 b6 4. g3 Bb7 5. Bg2 c5 6. d5 exd5 7. Ng5

overview: After 6.d5 exd5 White plays 7.Ng5, going for pressure on the d5 pawn and h7 and aiming at the quick queen and bishop tactics. Black can answer with ...h6 and ...Nc6 or ...d4, and usually ends with hanging pawns on c5 and d5 or an open centre. Read from the moves, as it is a rare variation.

white_ideas.idea: Hit d5 with Qb3 or Nf3 retreat and Bxd5
Use the g2 bishop and the knight on g5 against the centre pawns

black_ideas.idea: Kick the knight with ...h6 and develop ...Nc6
Keep c5 and d5 as hanging pawns or push ...d4

typical_structures.structure: Hanging pawns on c5 and d5 against a fianchettoed bishop

character.notes: Tactical early on, but both sides have clear, sound ways to play.

gambit.notes: The d5 pawn can be recaptured at once.

soundness.notes: Both sides have standard developing moves.

structure.notes: The c5 and d5 pawns are in tension and the centre is not settled.

approach.notes: A rare but respectable side line of the fianchetto QID.
